hook: Follow a radio feature with several voices and tell what the reporter states from what she only passes on.
intro: A radio feature from a Saturday morning in a city neighbourhood: a reporter describes the scene and links four voices — the volunteer Selin Demir, the sociologist Dr. Hartmann, the founder Werner Kolb, and the association itself, whose claim about its members she only passes on. On the radio you hear such a feature once and must keep track of who says what and in which mode: the reporter asserts in the indicative (Jeden Samstag trifft sich …), relays in the Konjunktiv I or II with a source (so heißt es im Verein, … seien; so Dr. Hartmann, … engagierten sich), and the interviewees speak for themselves. Feature reports end on the open problem — here the lack of young helpers who stay and a question nobody dares to answer.
tips[0].title: Asserted or relayed? Listen for the source
tips[0].text: so heißt es, so + name, laut, the Konjunktiv (seien, engagierten sich): the reporter is passing something on, not vouching for it. An item such as "Die Reporterin hat festgestellt, dass …" is then wrong, even if the content is right.
tips[0].trap: engagierten is Konjunktiv II here, standing in for the Konjunktiv I (engagieren), which would look identical to the indicative.
tips[0].check.why: so + a person and the Konjunktiv seien mark relayed speech: the claim belongs to the leader, not to the reporter.
tips[0].visual.rows[0].a: Die Halle ist seit Mai geschlossen.
tips[0].visual.rows[0].b: Die Stadt soll sie verkaufen wollen. / Laut Anwohnern sei …
tips[1].title: Qualifiers carry the answer
tips[1].text: Experts rarely say "yes" or "no"; they qualify: nicht nur … sondern auch, unabhängig von, allerdings, ergänzen, aber nicht ersetzen. Distractors take the half-sentence and drop the qualifier ("Ehrenamt ersetzt den Sozialstaat").
tips[1].check.why: nicht nur … sondern auch adds the second group; dropping that qualifier gives the wrong answer.
tips[2].title: The problem comes last
tips[2].text: Features move from scene to people to expert, and close on the unsolved problem. "Welche Sorge …?" and "Welches Problem …?" are answered in the last thirty seconds.
tips[2].check.why: Features close on the unsolved problem, here who will take over the shop, so the last lines answer the question about the open problem.
remember[0]: Reporter asserts in the indicative; so heißt es / so + Name / Konjunktiv = only relayed.
remember[1]: Qualifiers (unabhängig von, allerdings, ergänzen, aber nicht ersetzen) decide the item; the open problem comes at the end.
exam: Radio features with several voices are a standard listening text in the C1 exam — and on any Saturday-morning radio programme.
tips[0].check.q: 'Die Spenden, so die Leiterin, seien im Winter deutlich gestiegen.' Which statement is right?
tips[0].check.options[0]: The leader says donations rose; the reporter only passes it on.
tips[0].check.options[1]: The reporter has checked that donations rose.
tips[0].check.answer: The leader says donations rose; the reporter only passes it on.
tips[1].check.q: 'Das Projekt hilft nicht nur Älteren, sondern auch jungen Familien.' Which statement matches?
tips[1].check.options[0]: It helps older people and young families.
tips[1].check.options[2]: It helps young families instead of older people.
tips[1].check.answer: It helps older people and young families.
